title: Power Meter
statement: A science game multiplies a starting number `base` by itself `exp` times. The numbers get huge, so the game only shows the remainder after dividing by 1,000,000,007. Return `base^exp mod 1,000,000,007`. `exp` can be up to a billion, so multiplying one step at a time is far too slow.
constraints: Take the remainder after every multiplication; in JavaScript, use BigInt or split the product, because products can exceed 2^53

answerKey.pattern: Divide and conquer: square the half power (fast exponentiation)
keyPoints: If exp is even, the answer is half * half; if odd, half * half * base
Take the remainder after each multiplication
The exponent halves each call, so there are about log2(exp) calls
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(log exp) for the call stack

hints: x^n = (x^(n/2))^2 when n is even; multiply by x once more when n is odd. Compute the half only once.
Keep every product under the modulus. In JavaScript, (a * b) can lose digits; BigInt(a) * BigInt(b) % MOD does not.
